system.name: SNIC
system.one_liner: an empirical characterization of off-path SmartNICs (SNIC), comparing their RDMA READ/WRITE datapath and latency against a direct-attached RNIC baseline

content.subject: comparing READ/WRITE round-trip datapaths through SNIC's extra PCIe switch hop versus RNIC's single-hop baseline path

elements.name: RNIC
elements.role: top lane: the on-board RNIC core issuing/completing the request

elements.name: Switch
elements.role: PCIe switch inside the SmartNIC, between the on-board RNIC and the host

elements.name: Host
elements.role: bottom lane: the host CPU/memory that ultimately holds the data

elements.name: PCIe1
elements.role: the PCIe hop between the SNIC's on-board RNIC and its internal switch

elements.name: PCIe0
elements.role: the PCIe hop between the switch (or RNIC, in the baseline panel) and the host

relations.what: READ request travels down from RNIC through the Switch to Host, crossing PCIe1 then PCIe0
READ's completion travels back up through the Switch to RNIC, crossing both PCIe hops a second time
WRITE request travels down from RNIC through the Switch to Host
WRITE's completion travels back up only as far as the Switch, omitting the final PCIe1 hop to RNIC

panels.label: SNIC
panels.differs: an extra Switch lane splits the path into two PCIe hops; READ crosses both hops twice, WRITE's return stops at the Switch

panels.label: RNIC
panels.differs: no Switch lane; RNIC and Host joined by a single PCIe0 hop, so READ and WRITE both round-trip with one crossing each way

content.key_idea: SNIC's extra internal PCIe switch adds a second PCIe hop that READ must cross twice round-trip, while WRITE saves one hop by completing at the switch instead of returning all the way to the RNIC core.
content.reading_order: left panel top-to-bottom (RNIC, Switch, Host) following the READ then WRITE zigzag arrows down and back up; then the same for the simpler right (RNIC baseline) panel

palette.used_for: blue 'READ' and 'WRITE' labels marking each traced request type
white fill of the small boxed 'RNIC / Switch' grouping rectangle on the SNIC side

style.stroke: thin black lines for lanes and the zigzag request/response arrows
style.arrows: thin black diagonal arrows with open/hollow triangular heads, zigzagging down then up between lanes

encoding.color_means: blue marks the READ and WRITE labels; all lanes, edges, and arrows are otherwise plain black
encoding.line_style_means: not applicable; all lines are solid black, undifferentiated by style
encoding.state_means: the two panels (SNIC vs RNIC) are told apart structurally, by the presence or absence of the Switch lane and a second PCIe hop label, not by colour or ghosting
encoding.marker_means: not applicable, no numbered or symbolic markers
encoding.emphasis: drawing WRITE's return arrow stopping at the Switch lane (instead of reaching RNIC, as READ's does) visually isolates the one-hop saving the text attributes to WRITE
reusable_patterns: a small swimlane diagram where the same two message types (READ, WRITE) are re-traced over a baseline path and a path with one extra hop inserted, so the reader can count crossings directly
weaknesses: with no colour or label distinguishing the down-arrow from the up-arrow of a round trip, the reader must follow arrowheads carefully to see which leg is outbound vs return

evidence: Compared to RNIC, READ on SNIC passes through the PCIe switch twice (see Figure 4).
the increased latency of WRITE on SNIC is lower than that of READ, because it omits one pass through PCIe
because requests still must go through the PCIe switch at PCIe1.

summary: This figure from the SmartNIC characterization paper compares the READ/WRITE execution datapath of an off-path SmartNIC (SNIC) against a direct-attached RNIC baseline. In the SNIC panel, an extra on-board Switch lane sits between the RNIC core and the Host, splitting the path into two PCIe hops (PCIe1, PCIe0); a READ request travels down through both hops to the Host and back up through both a second time, while a WRITE's completion returns only as far as the Switch, skipping the final PCIe1 hop back to the RNIC core. In the RNIC panel, RNIC and Host are joined directly by a single PCIe0 hop, so both READ and WRITE round-trip with only one PCIe crossing each way. The extra switch hop is exactly why SNIC's measured READ/WRITE latency exceeds RNIC's, and why WRITE is cheaper than READ on SNIC.
summary_zh: 该图对比旁路SmartNIC(SNIC)与直连RNIC的READ/WRITE执行数据通路：SNIC一侧多了一层片上Switch，路径分为PCIe1、PCIe0两段，READ往返各需两次穿越，而WRITE的完成只回到Switch层，省去最后一次PCIe1；RNIC一侧只有一段PCIe0，READ/WRITE往返各穿越一次，这正是SNIC延迟高于RNIC、且WRITE比READ更快的原因。
notes: Corrected content.base from prior 'component' to 'timeline': the figure is a swimlane/sequence-style diagram (named horizontal lanes plus diagonal message arrows over an implicit time axis), matching the same paper's and corpus's convention for this base value rather than a components-and-connectors diagram. layout.panels is kept at 1 to mirror the index's measured single-panel count, even though content.panels lists 2 semantic alternatives (SNIC vs RNIC), consistent with the schema's index-derived layout fields. delta_marking is set to 'none' since the SNIC/RNIC difference is conveyed by an added lane and hop label rather than by colour, ghosting, or another highlighting device.
